pr_body:
Add support for the PG Julian Day date part.

This turned out to be annoying and time-consuming because JDs are `DOUBLE` 
and every other date part is `BIGINT`. The approach is to separate the two types of return values 
and disallow mixing (i.e., reading the date part from another column). Structs can still have `julian`
fields with type `DOUBLE`.

It was also not possible to use the rewrite rules to map `DATE_PART('Julian', <expr>)` to `JULIAN(<expr>)` because the return type changes and downstream code did not like that.

fixes #2827

issue_context.title: Postgres date part compatibility
comments: Giving up on `julian` for now because it is a floating point value.
This issue is stale because it has been open 90 days with no activity. Remove stale label or comment or this will be closed in 30 days.

review_comments: The cast will throw if it's not the right type, can we check if the type matches and return false before doing this?

This is a good point, but I looked at a _lot_ of other functions, and they all do this. Seems like something we should take a pass over to get them all. Right now, you can't even ask if the type is correct(!)

Can we explicitly number them?
Or maybe just a comment above JULIAN_DAY indicating this is where the DOUBLE parts start?

Yeah it's old school, but a standard C/C++ idiom.  The main reason I'm using it is that the exit conditions get more complex as you go down.  I could copy and paste the default return three times but that seemed bloated.
